title: playbook.json
description: A repo's declaration for the agent-ready repo playbook (devtools/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md). Fields are closed: an unknown key fails. There is no version pin: one rule set applies to every repo at release (private-repo).

ci.description: What the repo's CI needs on a CI host. The ship queue reads these at the job's base sha in place of the ship_ci_tool, ship_ci_service, ship_ci_secret, ship_ci_doppler, ship_ci_path, ship_ci_evidence and ship_ci_arch keys of .tree-guard.conf, which are then ignored with a warning (devtools/ship-queue/README.md, The declaration).

tools.description: NAME[@RANGE]: a tool of devtools/ship-queue/ci-hosts.json, beyond the hosts' base tools.

settings.description: The repo's CI settings: each NAME lists the tools (NAME[@RANGE] of devtools/ship-queue/ci-hosts.json) every run of that setting needs on its host. The repo's ship_ci_needs step prints the settings one job's CI uses, and the queue routes that job only to a host with the declared tools and those settings' tools (private-repo).

services.description: A compose service the CI needs; a remote CI host starts exactly these.

secrets.description: A vendor token the host hands the CI step (ship-queue's ci_secret_item names its 1Password item).

doppler.description: PROJECT/CONFIG: a Doppler config the queue host mints a short-lived read token for during the CI (ship_ci_doppler; private-repo).

paths.description: A directory the CI writes, relative to each CI host's data root ($SHIP_QUEUE_DATA_ROOT).

arch.description: x86_64, aarch64 or riscv64, as uname -m names it on Linux: the ship queue runs the CI only on a host of one of these (ship_ci_arch; private-repo). Absent: any host.

evidence.description: A path in the job tree that a failed run's evidence lives in (test traces, screenshots, lane logs). After a failed run on a CI host the ship queue brings it back to jobs/<id>/evidence/<host>/ before the run's worktree goes (private-repo).

path.description: A repo-relative path: no leading /, no .. segment.

baseline.description: A repo path to this contract's Baseline file.

command.description: The repo's line count (private-repo): it prints one JSON object, {"<file>": <code lines>}, covering every source file in the scope; an allowlisted function's own count is the key "<file>#<function>". The playbook holds each file to 500 code lines (and 500 raw lines, which it counts itself).

exempt.description: The repo's exempt places beyond the host's list (tests, drills, migrations, generated, CI files): each a regex of repo paths with the reason it is exempt. One scope and one 500-line limit apply to every repo (private-repo).

migrator.description: The repo's migration runner format and record table (private-repo): raw, drizzle, prisma, alembic, sqlx, or flyway.

protection.description: The member-data guards: the setting a migration sets before a protected write, and the guard functions' name prefix.

code.description: Runtime code directories that may not change the schema (and are read for TRUNCATE when listed in truncate).

truncate.description: Directories read for refused TRUNCATE statements.

scripts.description: Scripts and ops directories that may not alter or misquote an app table.

replay.description: How the migrations replay into a throwaway database for schema comparison (private-repo, #404, #771). `command` applies every migration with the repo's own runner, connecting through DATABASE_URL and the fleet shape's database env vars. `engine` is postgres (throwaway Postgres container; default when a Postgres image or dependency is present), sqlite (throwaway SQLite database file; default when SQLite is detected), or command (command prints the replayed schema JSON on stdout).

engine.description: How the migrations replay: postgres (throwaway Postgres container), sqlite (throwaway SQLite database file), or command (command prints the replayed schema JSON on stdout).

image.description: A Postgres-family image with every extension the migrations create, for example pgvector/pgvector:pg16.

database.description: The database name the migrations run in (default replay).

extensions.description: Extensions created before the first migration, for a system whose runner or platform creates them outside the migrations.

lint.description: The repo's migration lint (private-repo), for example squawk with its own config: run on the commit going in with PLAYBOOK_BASE and PLAYBOOK_MIGRATIONS_NEW (the new migration files, one per line); it must exit 0.

render.description: For migrations that are not SQL files (private-repo): prints the SQL the migration PLAYBOOK_MIGRATION (a repo path) runs, for the static rules; for example `alembic upgrade <down>:<rev> --sql` behind a repo script.

reads.description: The repo's command that prints the env names its code reads, as {"NAME": ["file", ...]} (private-repo, PLAYBOOK §1.2)

command.description: The umbrella generator command; null when the repo has no generator (then no file may carry a GENERATED marker).

source.description: The client source the whole-tree scan reads, as a regex of repo paths.

ledger.description: The walk ledger: each action's last recorded walk pass.

walk_baseline.description: The Baseline of entries not yet walked; its entries' issue names the ledger.

root.description: The folder the declaration's module paths are relative to.

held_back.description: The repo's held-back feature declaration ({features: {name: {modules}}}): an action whose featureFlag names a listed feature, with every use of its testID in that feature's declared modules, is walked when the feature turns on, not before it merges (exp#4000). Known from playbook 4; a host built before private-repo refuses it by schema.

chokepoint.description: True when the repository enforces user actions at component or type choke points (e.g. action: ActionId in contracts.design.ui), eliminating whole-tree AST crawler overhead.

floors.description: Declared runtime entity hydration floors for actions and journeys: maps action patterns or IDs to minimum required populated entity counts (e.g. {"profile:*": {"proofs": 1}}).

evidence.description: The repo's action-to-test evidence (private-repo): `run` prints {"tests": [{"file", "line", "title", "kind": "e2e"|"component", "actions": [ids], "selectors": [testIDs]}]}; `tests` is a regex of the test files it reads (a change to one runs the actions check).

slot_calls.description: Functions or hooks that name an appearance slot (e.g. skinSlotHasArt, useSkinSlot; private-repo).

system.description: The design system's folder (private-repo): a script under it that renders nothing is token source like the token module. Never a whole client scope, never holding the UI package.

client.description: The client code: path prefixes ending in /, or single files (private-repo).

content_values.description: Authored rendering data within client scope (private-repo). Changes the classification of content values, never file coverage: DOM/native UI styles, CSS, embedded HTML and visitor interactions remain checked. The reason and scope are reviewed with declaration changes.

touch_calls.description: The UI package's functions or hooks whose result, spread on an element or as its hitSlop, gives it the 48dp touch target (private-repo; e.g. useTouchTarget).

command.description: The repo's declared design check command (required for `playbook check design`; private-repo): run on the commit going in with PLAYBOOK_BASE; it must exit 0 and emit {"findings": [{"rule", "file", "line", "text", "message"}], "files"?: <int>} on stdout.

chokepoint.description: True when the repository enforces design tokens and UI primitives at component choke points.

tools.description: The repo's declared checks (PLAYBOOK §14; private-repo): the playbook runs each step and requires exit 0, and every language in the tree has a step of each class it needs. It holds no tool, config or Baseline.

optimization.description: Optimization budgets (PLAYBOOK §11): `file` (the budgets) and `receipts` (the ledger the repo's measurement run writes) or `measuredBy` (the merge gate measures, and no ledger is committed), with an optional `baseline`; or `none`, the reason a repo with no route, job or action has nothing to budget. The gate refuses a mix.

measuredBy.description: In place of `receipts`: the repo's merge gate is the measurement run, and the repo holds no receipts file. Accepted only where `.tree-guard.conf` declares `ship_merge_gate` and `ship_pass_record=merge`.

command.description: A nonblank command the playbook runs with bash in the checkout (private-repo): the repo's own tool and config. It must exit 0; it reads, never writes.

step.description: One declared check (private-repo): the playbook runs `run` on the commit going in and requires exit 0. Which tool, config and rules are the repo's.

name.description: The step's name, unique in the list; results are `tools <name>`.

class.description: The class of check: every language the tree holds needs the classes pb_languages names for it (lint and deadcode for every language; typecheck for a statically typed language), and a tracked lockfile needs deps.

languages.description: The languages the step checks (pb_languages names); empty for a deps step.

config.description: The config files the command reads: each must exist, and a change to one is reported in the result.
